title: Acceptance of Letters Patent
subtitle: The reciprocal instrument: the appointee's own act, without which the dignity is not constituted

blocks.text: The counterpart to a grant. Under the authentication article of every instrument in this corpus, Letters Patent become effective upon declaration of the constituting Act, acceptance by the appointee, signature by the Sovereign, signature or attestation by the appointee, and application of the Seal. Acceptance is therefore constitutive, not ceremonial, and this plate is the instrument that supplies it — carrying the continuing vow and a confirmation of style.

blocks.caption: Acceptance of Letters Patent — The reciprocal instrument: the appointee's own act, without which the dignity is not constituted
blocks.explanation: This is the article that makes the corpus non-coercive in practice rather than only in principle. A dignity that required no acceptance would be an imposition however carefully its non-suzerainty clauses were drafted. Because acceptance is a condition of effect, declining is a complete and internally provided answer: the instrument simply never constitutes.
